text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Incident Drill started by @Owen Phillips in #incidents (Private staging). Objective: validate Private min-pack alerting (SLO burn + critical availability).

Owen Phillips: Kicking off the drill in private-staging-03. We’re going to induce 5xx on the gateway for ~10m. Expectation: `Gateway5xxHigh` + SLO burn should page (sev2) to oncall within 5m. I’m not seeing anything yet.

Sean Gallagher: Copy. Starting timer. Please drop a note when you flip the fault on.

Owen Phillips: Fault on now. Simulating upstream failure (gateway returning 503). RPS ~40.

Dev Patel: Watching the oncall channel + PagerDuty. Nothing yet.

Allison Grant: Also watching Grafana alert list in staging (the customer-managed-style stack). I’m not seeing the min-pack rule groups.

Sean Gallagher: If we don’t page, treat as real failure. First triage: are rules even loaded in Prometheus? Check Prometheus UI → Status → Rules.

Owen Phillips: Looking at Prometheus UI now. Under “Rules” I only see kube rules + node rules. No `redwood-private-min-pack` group. That seems…bad.

Sergio Costa: That points to PrometheusRule not being selected by the operator or rule parsing failing. Can someone run:
`kubectl get prometheusrules -A | grep -i redwood`

Bruno Silva: On it.

Bruno Silva:
```
$ kubectl get prometheusrules -A | grep -i redwood
redwood-private-observability  redwood-min-pack-slo-alerts     11m
redwood-private-observability  redwood-min-pack-health-alerts   11m
redwood-private-observability  redwood-min-pack-pipeline-alerts 11m
```
They exist.

Allison Grant: So Prometheus isn’t picking them up. What’s the Prometheus instance ruleSelector? (kube-prometheus-stack uses label selector by default)

Sergio Costa: +1. `kubectl describe prometheus -n monitoring <name>` and look at `ruleSelector` / `ruleNamespaceSelector`.

Bruno Silva:
```
$ kubectl get prometheus -n monitoring
prometheus-k8s   1/1   22h

$ kubectl describe prometheus -n monitoring prometheus-k8s | sed -n '/Rule Selector/,+12p'
Rule Selector:
  Match Labels:
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
Rule Namespace Selector:
  Match Labels:
    kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
```

Sergio Costa: Aha. Our PrometheusRules are in namespace `redwood-private-observability`, not `monitoring`, and Prometheus has `ruleNamespaceSelector` pinned to monitoring only. That would explain “no rules loaded.”

Markus Klein: This matches what we’ve seen in a couple Private installs: some customers run Prometheus in `monitoring` but want apps in their own namespaces. If we require rules in monitoring, we need to be explicit + provide install-time wiring.

Allison Grant: Wait, but our install guide draft implied rules can be deployed alongside Redwood components (same namespace). That’s incompatible with this Prometheus config.

Sean Gallagher: For the drill, quick fix is to install the PrometheusRules into `monitoring` or widen the selector. What’s easier in staging?

Bruno Silva: Widening selector requires editing Prometheus CR (cluster-level), might be more invasive. For now I can copy/apply PrometheusRule manifests into `monitoring`.

Sergio Costa: Let’s do the minimal patch: apply same PrometheusRule resources into `monitoring` namespace and add `release: kube-prometheus-stack` label so they’re selected.

Sahana Iyer: Before we patch, can we capture current state for the postmortem? Screenshot or at least the Prometheus rule list being empty for our groups.

Owen Phillips: Grabbed screenshot of Status→Rules showing no redwood groups.

Bruno Silva: Applying patch now.

Bruno Silva:
```
# export existing rules
kubectl get prometheusrule -n redwood-private-observability redwood-min-pack-slo-alerts -o yaml > /tmp/slo.yaml
# (edited namespace to monitoring and added label release=kube-prometheus-stack)
kubectl apply -f /tmp/slo.yaml

kubectl get prometheusrule -n monitoring | grep redwood
redwood-min-pack-slo-alerts   1m
```
Doing same for health + pipeline.

Allison Grant: Refreshing Prometheus UI… I now see `redwood-min-pack-slo` group. Good sign.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Now, are alerts evaluating? Check `/api/v1/rules` and also `ALERTS` series.

Owen Phillips: In Prometheus graph, `ALERTS{alertname="Gateway5xxHigh"}` is now showing `pending`.

Dev Patel: PagerDuty still quiet but if it’s pending we should page shortly.

Sean Gallagher: Keep fault on until it goes firing + page is received.

Owen Phillips: Still faulting.

Allison Grant: `Gateway5xxHigh` flipped to `firing` in Prometheus UI at 4m30s after patch.

Dev Patel: Pager received (sev2) in PD at 1708981123. :+1: So the drill failure is confirmed: rules weren’t being loaded at all.

Sean Gallagher: Root cause: Prometheus ruleNamespaceSelector limited to `monitoring`, our pack installed rules in app namespace. That’s a pretty common Prometheus Operator posture.

Sergio Costa: Also we should confirm label selector. Bruno added `release=kube-prometheus-stack` manually; our chart should support `additionalLabels` and docs should call out required labels when Prometheus uses ruleSelector.

Allison Grant: This should be a “supported install” requirement: either (a) customer Prometheus selects the pack namespace, or (b) we deploy PrometheusRule into monitoring namespace, or (c) we provide a documented method to set selectors.

Markus Klein: Strong preference from Solutions side: don’t ask customers to edit their Prometheus CR during go-live unless absolutely necessary. We should default to installing rules into `monitoring` when we detect kube-prometheus-stack / Prometheus Operator, with override knob.

Bruno Silva: For private installer, we can:
- add `--observability.rulesNamespace` defaulting to `monitoring` (if present), else fall back to Redwood namespace
- add `--observability.prometheusRuleSelectorLabels` or `--observability.prometheusReleaseLabel` helper (so we can match `release: kube-prometheus-stack`)

Sahana Iyer: And validation harness should fail fast if rule groups aren’t loaded. We can check:
- Prometheus API `/api/v1/rules` contains group name prefix `redwood-min-pack-`
- Or query `prometheus_rule_group_last_evaluation_timestamp_seconds` / `prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total` if available
- At minimum, count of groups > 0

Sergio Costa: +1. Also add a “missing signals” alert group item specifically for “no min-pack rule groups loaded” (ironically needs to be loaded, but we can piggyback on kube-prometheus-stack’s built-in alert `PrometheusRuleFailures` if present).

Allison Grant: There’s also `prometheus_operator_reconcile_errors_total` in the operator metrics we can use to detect selector mismatch / reconcile issues.

Sean Gallagher: Action items:
1) Chart/pack: ability to target namespace for PrometheusRules + add required labels (owner @Sergio Costa)
2) Installer: detect/promote recommended defaults + expose flags (owner @Bruno Silva)
3) Validation: add post-install check for rule groups loaded and alerting pipeline health (owner @Sahana Iyer)
4) Docs: explicitly document Prometheus Operator selectors + kube-prometheus-stack defaults + troubleshooting steps (owner: loop in Kira/Elliot; I’ll ping separately)
5) SRE: update drill checklist to include “verify rules loaded” step before inducing failures (owner @Sean Gallagher)

Owen Phillips: For completeness, triage steps we followed (for the runbook):
- Grafana alert list empty → check Prometheus UI Status→Rules
- `kubectl get prometheusrules -A` to confirm CRs exist
- `kubectl describe prometheus` to inspect `ruleSelector` + `ruleNamespaceSelector`
- Patch/apply rules into selected namespace + ensure selector labels match
- Re-check Prometheus UI for group presence → confirm `ALERTS` series

Dev Patel: Support angle: add this to “common pitfalls” (rules installed but not selected). We should include the exact commands + what “good” looks like.

Allison Grant: One more follow-up: we should standardize the naming prefix across all groups so the validation can be simple and robust (`redwood-min-pack-*`).

Sergio Costa: Ack. I’ll open a PR to make rule namespace configurable in the helm chart and to allow `additionalLabels` for PrometheusRule.

Bruno Silva: I’ll file an installer issue to add detection for kube-prometheus-stack and default rulesNamespace=monitoring + release label. Also we should consider customers who run Prometheus outside the cluster; for them we likely ship YAML and they apply it wherever.

Sean Gallagher: Drill complete. Logging incident-like outcome: “Alert failed to fire due to rule loading (namespace selector mismatch).” Thanks all. Let’s keep the staging patch minimal and revert after we’ve got a proper change in the pack.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Incident Drill marked resolved by @Sean Gallagher. Next step: follow-ups tracked in eng workstream.
